content:
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Primary endpoint ORR may not capture immunotherapeutic response patterns",
      "quote": "The primary endpoint of the study is the ORR, defined as the proportion of subjects with a confirmed objective response of CR or PR based on RECIST v1.1 as determined by Blinded Independent Central Review (BICR).",
      "page": 33,
      "section": "2.2.1",
      "category": "advisory",
      "severity": "advisory",
      "explanation": "For immunotherapies, RECIST v1.1 may underestimate responses due to pseudoprogression; iRECIST is often preferred for primary endpoint.",
      "fix": "Consider using iRECIST or a composite endpoint that includes immune-related response criteria for the primary endpoint."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inclusion criterion for BRAF V600 mutation status may be overly restrictive",
      "quote": "Patients with BRAF V600 mutations who refuse a BRAF inhibitor will not be eligible.",
      "page": 38,
      "section": "4.1.2",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "This excludes patients who may have contraindications or intolerances to BRAF inhibitors, potentially limiting enrollment and generalizability.",
      "fix": "Allow enrollment of patients who refuse BRAF inhibitors if they have documented reasons (e.g., contraindication) and discuss with Medical Monitor."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inclusion criterion for prior radiation target lesion may be ambiguous",
      "quote": "Documented disease progression in any lesion that was previously radiated in order to serve as a target lesion.",
      "page": 38,
      "section": "4.1.4c",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The wording is unclear: it could mean that a previously radiated lesion must have progressed to be eligible as a target lesion, but it is not specified whether this is required for all target lesions or just one. This ambiguity may lead to inconsistent interpretation and amendments.",
      "fix": "Clarify that at least one measurable lesion not previously radiated must be present, or specify that previously radiated lesions must have documented progression to be considered measurable."
    },
    {
      "title": "Exclusion criterion for active autoimmune disease may be too broad",
      "quote": "Active autoimmune disease that has required systemic treatment in past 2 years; replacement therapy is not considered a form of systemic treatment.",
      "page": 40,
      "section": "4.2.11",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The 2-year window may exclude patients with well-controlled autoimmune conditions (e.g., hypothyroidism on replacement) that are not considered active, but the wording could be misinterpreted. Also, it does not specify which autoimmune diseases are excluded (e.g., vitiligo is often allowed).",
      "fix": "Specify exceptions for common autoimmune conditions like vitiligo, psoriasis not requiring systemic treatment, and controlled thyroid disease."
    },
    {
      "title": "Safety monitoring for adrenal insufficiency is only in a NOTE, not in the Schedule of Activities",
      "quote": "Subjects previously treated with a CTLA-4–blocking antibody, subjects receiving corticosteroids with daily doses > 5 mg and ≤ 10 mg of prednisone equivalent for > 2 weeks, and subjects with clinical symptoms and/or laboratory findings suggesting risk for adrenal insufficiency should undergo diagnostic tests for adrenal insufficiency via local laboratory.",
      "page": 39,
      "section": "4.2.6",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol mentions diagnostic tests for adrenal insufficiency but does not specify which tests (e.g., cortisol, ACTH) or include them in the Schedule of Activities, which may lead to inconsistent monitoring and missing safety data.",
      "fix": "Add specific adrenal function tests (e.g., morning cortisol, ACTH stimulation test) to the Schedule of Activities for at-risk patients."
    },
    {
      "title": "Exclusion criterion for HIV/HBV/HCV is vague and may cause delays",
      "quote": "Known or suspected active infection with human immunodeficiency virus, hepatitis B virus, or hepatitis C virus (testing is not required unless suspected).",
      "page": 40,
      "section": "4.2.16",
      "category": "amendment_risk",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The phrase 'suspected' is subjective and may lead to inconsistent screening practices. Also, not requiring testing may miss asymptomatic infections, which could be a safety concern with immunotherapy.",
      "fix": "Require routine screening for HIV, HBV, and HCV at baseline, and define 'suspected' more objectively (e.g., based on risk factors or symptoms)."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inclusion criterion for tissue biopsy may be impractical and cause enrollment delays",
      "quote": "A fresh tissue biopsy (within 90 days before the start of study treatment) is preferred but an archival sample is acceptable (as a substitute) if no intervening therapy was received.",
      "page": 38,
      "section": "4.1.5",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Requiring a fresh biopsy within 90 days may be burdensome for patients with refractory melanoma, and the archival sample condition (no intervening therapy) may be difficult to meet, potentially delaying enrollment.",
      "fix": "Extend the biopsy window or allow archival samples regardless of intervening therapy if adequate tissue is available."
    },
    {
      "title": "Exclusion criterion for prior radiation within 2 weeks may be too restrictive for this population",
      "quote": "Received radiation therapy (or other nonsystemic therapy) within 2 weeks before first dose of study treatment on W1D1.",
      "page": 39,
      "section": "4.2.2",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "Patients with refractory melanoma may have had recent palliative radiation; a 2-week washout may be unnecessarily long and could exclude patients who would otherwise benefit.",
      "fix": "Consider shortening the washout to 1 week or allowing radiation to non-target lesions with recovery to Grade ≤1."
    }
  ]
}
